newsitem.title: USA: Nigerian human rights award winner missing.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian human rights award winner missing.

text.p: A human rights activist who has opposed Nigeria's military government and was to be honored at a ceremony in Boston was missing on Sunday, a spokeswoman for the event said.

Innocent Chukwuma, 30, a project director for the Civli Liberties Organization, Nigeria's oldest and largest human rights association, was scheduled to arrive in the United States on Friday for the 1996 Reebok Human Rights Award ceremonies this week. He never made it, according to event spokeswoman Kathleen Crocker.

"He was supposed to fly from Nigeria to Ghana, then to London and Washington and arrive here last night," said Crocker. "He never arrived in this country and we're still trying to track him down. We don't what's happened, whether he's been arrested or what."

Chukwuma has been jailed twice in the past for challenging the policies of successive military regimes in Nigeria, said Crocker. He was scheduled to be one of four human rights activists to receive the 1996 Reebok Human Rights Award at a ceremony on Wednesday, the day after Human Rights Day.
Africa's most populous nation has been under fire from Western countries for human rights abuses and lack of democracy.
